english: It's enough for him to apologize.
tip: 'Basta que' (it is enough that) triggers the subjunctive: 'peca', not pede.

english: If you need anything, I'm available.
tip: 'Caso' means if and takes the subjunctive: 'caso precise' = if you need. It is more formal than 'se'.

target: Eu quero experimentar a comida baiana.
english: I want to try Bahian food.
tip: 'Experimentar' means to try or taste something new: 'experimentar a comida' = try the food. Not the same as tentar.

target: Ele nos convidou para o churrasco.
english: He invited us to the barbecue.
tip: 'Convidar' uses 'para' for the event: 'convidou para o churrasco' = invited us to the barbecue.

target: A gente os encontrou na praia.
english: We found them at the beach.
tip: The object pronoun os in os encontrou reads formal; everyday Brazilian speech says encontrou eles instead.

target: A gente lhes explicou a situação.
english: We explained the situation to them.
tip: 'Lhes' means to them and marks the indirect object: 'lhes explicou' = explained to them.

target: Eu vou te buscar às oito.
english: I'll pick you up at eight.
tip: With 'vou' plus an infinitive, the pronoun sits between them: 'vou te buscar' = I'll pick you up.

target: A gente nos conheceu na faculdade.
english: We met in college.
tip: 'Conhecer' means to meet for the first time: 'nos conheceu na faculdade' = we met in college. Reencounter is encontrar.

target: Não acho que ele venha hoje.
english: I don't think he's coming today.
tip: acho que takes the indicative, but negating it to não acho que flips the verb to the subjunctive: venha.

target: A gente faz amizade fácil no Brasil.
english: We make friends easily in Brazil.
tip: 'Fazer amizade' means 'to make friends.' Brazilians use many 'fazer' expressions: fazer compras (shop), fazer fila (queue), fazer sentido (make sense).

target: É estranho que ele não tenha ligado.
english: It's strange that he hasn't called.
tip: é estranho que takes the subjunctive tenha ligado even though the event is real; the emotion triggers it, not doubt.

english: Take good care of your little brother.
tip: 'Cuide' is the polite command, borrowed from the subjunctive: 'cuide bem' = take good care. Casual speech says 'cuida'.

target: Eu não a vi na festa.
english: I didn't see her at the party.
tip: 'A' = her (formal direct object). 'Não a vi' = I didn't see her. Formal; spoken: 'não vi ela.'

target: Eu lhe garanto que vai dar certo.
english: I guarantee you it will work out.
tip: lhe here means 'to you', matching você; it isn't always 'to him'. Eu lhe garanto is 'I assure you'.

english: Maybe he'll resign.
tip: Talvez triggers the subjunctive, so pedir becomes peça, not pede. The mood marks the outcome as uncertain.

english: Look how cool!
tip: In olha só, só isn't 'only'; it just adds emphasis, so olha só means 'just look'.

english: Hold this for me.
tip: Casual Brazilian commands use the he/she form: segura, not the textbook segure.

english: Don't throw food away.
tip: Negative commands switch to subjunctive endings: não jogue, not jogar. An a-verb like jogar takes -e.

english: Let me finish speaking.
tip: Colloquial deixa eu plus an infinitive means let me: deixa eu terminar. Careful grammar would say deixe-me terminar.

target: Fico feliz que você esteja aqui.
english: I'm glad you're here.
tip: Feelings take the subjunctive after que: fico feliz que você esteja, not está.

english: Be careful on the road.
tip: Tomar cuidado means be careful, literally take care: toma cuidado is the everyday warning.

english: I hope everything works out.
tip: Tomara que means let's hope and always takes the subjunctive: tomara que dê, from the verb dar.

english: Call me when you arrive.
tip: For a future when, use the future subjunctive: quando chegar means when you arrive, not quando chega.

english: Confirm your reservation in advance.
tip: Formal commands use the subjunctive form: Confirme. The informal version to a friend would be confirma.

english: Park the car right here.
tip: After a place word, mesmo means right or exactly: aqui mesmo means right here.

english: Order an Uber for us.
tip: A gente means we or us in casual speech: pra gente means for us here.

english: We would cook for everyone.
tip: The conditional would adds -ria endings to the whole infinitive: cozinhar plus íamos gives cozinharíamos.

target: A menos que você estude, vai reprovar.
english: Unless you study, you'll fail.
tip: A menos que means unless and always takes the subjunctive: a menos que você estude, not estuda.

english: I hope I pass the exam.
tip: Oxalá means hopefully, from Arabic, and forces the subjunctive: oxalá eu passe, not passo.

english: Pull the door to open it.
tip: Puxar means to pull, not to push: puxa a porta. The push sign says empurre.
